title: Clean body, clean place
hook: wudu, clean clothes, a clean spot, and the idea behind them

segments.voice: Yesterday: niyyah, the intention, formed in the heart. Your line was mean it first. Behind us now: a small band crossing the sea to a just king, a year of grief, a bloody road out of Ta'if, a night journey, a migration, a camel kneeling in Medina.

A man rolls up his sleeves at work, in the restroom, and washes his hands, his mouth, his face, his arms to the elbow, wipes his head, washes his feet. A coworker walks in and looks a little puzzled. He's not being fussy. He's getting ready. Before anyone says a word of the prayer, the cleanness comes first.
screen: `A SINK AT WORK.` → `A COWORKER LOOKS PUZZLED.` → `HE'S GETTING READY.`

segments.voice: The Arabic word is taharah, purity or cleanness. Books of Islamic law put it ahead of the chapter on prayer, because the prayer isn't valid without it. It has three layers. First, the body. For the daily prayers that usually means wudu, the washing the Qur'an itself describes in Surah al-Ma'idah: wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet up to the ankles. After some things, like sleep or using the toilet, wudu needs renewing. After others, like sex, a full bath is needed, called ghusl. Second, the clothes: clean of things like urine or blood. Third, the place: a clean spot to stand on. That's what a prayer rug is for. It isn't holy in itself, just a clean surface you can carry anywhere. Here's the surprise. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said, in a hadith in Bukhari, that the whole earth had been made for him a place of prayer and a means of purification. A field, a parking lot, the edge of an airport gate: any clean ground will do. When there's no water, or water would harm you, there's tayammum: you touch clean earth or dust and wipe your face and hands. The idea behind it all is in a short hadith in Sahih Muslim: purity is half of faith. Not a rule tacked on to the prayer. Half of the thing itself. Some scholars read it as outside and inside together: the water on the skin, and the turning of the heart it's meant to go with.
screen: `TAHARAH — BEFORE EVERYTHING ELSE.` · `THE BODY, THE CLOTHES, THE PLACE.` · `THE WHOLE EARTH, A PLACE OF PRAYER.` · `PURITY IS HALF OF FAITH.` · then, large: `OUTSIDE AND INSIDE TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Clear one small spot near you, a corner of the floor, a chair, a patch of desk, and if you have a clean cloth, a towel or a scarf, lay it down flat and smooth it with your hands. Sit near it, breathing slowly, and look: a small place where nothing is piled up. If you've done wudu before, notice where the water would go; if you pray, this is the kind of place you'd pray on.
Taharah. Cleanness of body, clothes and place, the half of faith that comes before the prayer. Today's word.
Your line: a clean corner. The prayer, step by step, starts here. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Before each prayer, Muslims make sure they are in wudu (the ritual washing of face, arms, head and feet), that their clothes are clean, and that they pray on a clean spot, often a prayer rug; with no water, they use tayammum with clean earth.
